notes: The supplied PDF has no readable inventory pages, so I could not read the real Element IDs.

Yellow 1x1 pieces (b10, b11): the 'lego-3070' id was rejected. They now use catalogue type lego-3005744 (yellow round 1x1 plate), the closest catalogue match. The picture could also show a flat 1x1 tile.

Flame (b15): I kept this part because the Batmobile does have a flame element. I could not find its Element ID, and lego-6126 is my best guess. It is probably still unverified. Please replace it with the Element ID from the inventory page.
lego-slope-grille and lego-fender-arch are placeholder ids for the same reason. The grille slopes and curved fender are real parts of this model.
b8:top.2 and b4:top.2 are each used once. b8 sits on both studs of b7, the flame sits on the grille b17, and b20 is joined to b19.
The step 1 base plate looks like a 3x4 plate. I used lego-3031 (4x4) as the closest match.
Which stud or port each piece sits on is approximate where the pictures are small. This applies most to the wheel holders in step 4 and the rear top pieces in steps 10-13.
Step 4 shows pins sticking out at both ends. I modelled them as two wheel-holder plates (front and rear), each with two pins, and put four wheels on those pins in step 14.
The two trans-red round plates seen in step 8 are attached to the underside of the base plate.
Step 7 builds a sub-assembly (a 1x4 plate with two yellow pieces and a curved fender) and then fits it on the front of the yellow plate.
